formNote: Mojidata IDS: ⿰亻言. The Shuowen: 信，誠也。从人从言 — “sincerity: from person and word.” A person standing by their word. It also means a letter.
summary: Good faith: a person standing by their word. Confucius said that without it he could not see how a person could get on. With 仁 義 禮 智 it makes the five constants, 五常.
placement: At the top of the disk, above 仁, where the band starts to lift toward the fold. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: A Person Without Good Faith
satellites.evidence: Analects 2.22: 人而無信，不知其可也。大車無輗，小車無軏，其何以行之哉 — “a person without good faith: I do not see how they can manage. A cart without its yoke-pin: how could it move?”

satellites.title: The Five Constants
satellites.evidence: Han Confucians named five constant virtues, 仁義禮智信, adding 信 to Mencius’s four. This system takes its name from them.
satellites.caveat: The attribution to Dong Zhongshu and the Han date are Baracus’s, from general knowledge.
gaps: Cite a Han primary source for 五常 (e.g. Dong Zhongshu, or the Baihu tong).
